lessons.title: Average Basics
lessons.concept: Average = Sum of values ÷ Number of values. Weighted average accounts for different group sizes.
lessons.worked_example: Mean monthly salary of 75 workers = 5680. Mean of 25 = 5400, of 30 = 5700. Remaining (20) = (5680×75 − 5400×25 − 5700×30)/20 = 6000.

lessons.title: Weighted Average
lessons.concept: Combined average = (sum of all values) / (total count), accounting for group sizes.
lessons.worked_example: Boys avg 71 (count b), girls avg 73 (count g). Combined = (71b+73g)/(b+g).
mistakes: Simple average of two group averages

practice.question: A weighted average differs from a simple average because it:

options.B: Assigns each value an importance (weight) before averaging

practice.explanation: Weighted averages multiply each value by its weight; when weights (e.g. group sizes) differ, the result differs from the unweighted mean.
